# Historical market fixtures

Audited 2026-10-07 against the official UTA documentation. All JSON files here
are **synthetic contract fixtures**, not captures of live exchange traffic.
Times/prices/IDs are authored test values, so their age says nothing about live
availability. Original bytes (including whitespace and newlines) are test inputs.

| Fixture | Classification | Purpose/source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `candles-exclusive.json` | Synthetic boundary scenario | Strict interior of a requested time window; not evidence that Bitget always excludes equality. [History candles](https://www.bitget.com/docs/catalog/market/market-data#get-klinecandlestick-history) |
| `candles-inclusive.json` | Synthetic boundary scenario | Provider includes candles equal to both requested bounds. The SDK must preserve them, not assume inclusive/exclusive equality. Same history-candles source. |
| `candles-rounded-extra.json` | Synthetic documented rounding scenario | An end bound 1 ms past an interval may produce an extra earlier interval; preserve all rows. Same history-candles source. |
| `liquidations-page-1.json`, `liquidations-page-2.json` | Partial observations, synthetic pagination | Exact amounts, millisecond event text, opaque cursor, repeated indistinguishable observations; no synthesized event identity. [Liquidations REST](https://www.bitget.com/docs/catalog/market/derivatives#get-liquidations-history) |
| `recent-fills.json` | Recent data only, synthetic | Execution/correlation IDs exceed float precision; size is quote coin for COIN-FUTURES, base coin otherwise. [Recent public fills](https://www.bitget.com/docs/catalog/market/market-data#get-recent-public-fills) |
| `rate-limit.json` | Synthetic API/HTTP error | Preserve error envelope bytes and existing rate-limit classifications. [UTA guide](https://www.bitget.com/docs/uta/quick-start) |
| `truncated.json` | Synthetic malformed body | A complete HTTP read can still contain invalid/truncated JSON: error with exact receipt, never success. |

## Audit and admission decisions

- `/api/v3/market/history-candles` is a separate deep-history route. Selectors:
  category, symbol, interval, type, startTime, endTime and limit. Request limit
  default/maximum 100; each requested time range may span at most 90 days but
  may reach older data. The prose says after/before without an explicit equality
  guarantee. Boundary fixtures therefore test transparent SDK behaviour for
  both interpretations, not live server assertions. No rounding, trimming,
  deduplication or inferred completeness is performed by the SDK.
- The public UTA market catalog exposes `/api/v3/market/fills` as recent fills,
  limit 100, without time selectors/cursor. No documented UTA public deep fills
  route was found. The official [private fill history](https://www.bitget.com/docs/catalog/trading/order-management#get-fill-history)
  is `/api/v3/trade/fills`, requires UTA trade read permission, and covers a
  90-day lookback in windows of at most 30 days, with cursor pagination. It is
  account history, not the public market tape. Classic v2 public fills-history
  exists but is a different API: [Classic futures market](https://www.bitget.com/docs/catalog/classic-contract-market/classic-contract-market).
  No public UTA historical fills method is fabricated or substituted.
- `/api/v3/market/liquidations` exposes category, optional symbol, limit up to
  100 and an opaque cursor. It covers only three recent days and may be delayed.
  The documented example contains symbol, side, price, amount and ts, without
  a stable execution/event ID. The REST contract does not specify amount units
  or aggregation/exhaustiveness. These remain unknown, not inherited from fills.
  The [June 2026 changelog](https://www.bitget.com/docs/uta/changelog/2026-06)
  limits the *WebSocket* liquidation channel to the largest long/short observation
  per symbol per second; that is not evidence of identical REST aggregation.
  `PartialLiquidations` explicitly prevents a complete-history claim; a cursor
  is pagination state, not event identity or a completeness watermark.

Oversize (bound + 1), interrupted body reads, cancellation and malformed data
are generated by tests rather than stored as multi-megabyte fixtures. Receipts
bound retained bytes, distinguish incomplete reads from decode errors, omit
headers/credentials/host, and copy mutable accessors.
